title: record:details' field-security fold keeps entries whose identity it cannot resolve — the same fail-open default objectui#8793 closed on related lists
body:
## The census that produced this

objectui#8793 closed a fail-open default in `record:related_list`'s field-security
fold: an entry whose identity did not resolve was KEPT, so it escaped both
`enforceFieldSecurity` and `redactFields`. The dispatch for that card asked
whether sibling filters carry the same shape. They were read at the source, and
one does.

**`packages/plugin-detail/src/renderers/record-details.tsx`, `filterList`** — the
same branch, byte for byte in structure:

```ts
const fieldName = (entry: any): string | null => columnIdentity(entry) ?? null;
// ...
return list.filter((e) => {
  const n = fieldName(e);
  return n ? allowed.has(n) : true;   // identity unresolved => KEPT
});
```

Its identity reader is even narrower than the related list's: `columnIdentity`
alone, with no `key` tail fallback. So every entry that is not a bare string,
`{ field }`, `{ name }` or `{ fieldName }` takes the else-branch and is kept
unfiltered whenever the block is enforcing FLS or redacting.

**The third renderer on the same family fails CLOSED already**, and is worth
recording as the contrast: `record-highlights.tsx` normalizes its `fields` and
then drops every entry without a non-empty string `name` BEFORE the allow-list is
applied, so an unnamed entry cannot reach the filter at all.

## ⚠️ What is measured here, and what is NOT

- **Measured**: the shape. The fail-open branch is there, read at the source.
- **NOT measured**: whether it is an EXPOSURE. What made objectui#8793 a data
  leak rather than a filtering nit was a second read point — `RelatedList` renders
  a column as `accessorKey || columnIdentity(c)`, so the entry the filter could
  not name was rendered anyway, with its real value. `record:details` hands its
  entries to `DetailSection`, which reads `field.name`; an entry carrying only
  `accessorKey` may simply render nothing. A probe against the details renderer
  produced a placeholder row rather than a value, but that probe could not get an
  ordinary `{ field: 'x' }` entry to render either, so it is inconclusive about
  the real read path and is reported as such rather than dressed up.

⇒ the first job on this card is that measurement: drive `record:details` the way a
record page actually drives it, author an entry the fold cannot name, and see
whether a VALUE reaches the screen. If it does, this is objectui#8793 again in a
second block. If it does not, it is still a fail-open default on a security
boundary and still wants closing, but its priority is different and the PR body
should say which of the two it turned out to be.

Filed by the dev seat working objectui#8793; the fix there stayed on the one
branch its card names.
